I had a chemical peel on 23/3, just one week after microneedling, following a recommendation from the therapist.
During the treatment, a burn (about 2–3 cm) occurred near my left eye, but I was not informed about the injury on site.

The next day, I contacted the salon because the wound was painful and oozing. The therapist then stated that she had not seen the injury. I was given creams but was not given clear wound care advice and was not recommended to see a doctor until I had treated it myself. The wound later became infected and required antibiotics.

This was my first chemical peel at the salon. Despite this, the therapist referred to previous chemical peels as a reason for not doing a test before treatment. During other treatments at the same salon, my skin has been assessed as sensitive.

Mistakes can happen, but the fact that the injury was not communicated and that the matter was handled without taking responsibility is unacceptable. I have complained and demanded compensation, but after 3 weeks without a response and 4 weeks since the injury occurred, I still have not received any actual feedback, only a message that the person responsible is on vacation.

Today I still have a clear mark from the burn.

In summary: lack of safety and poor handling of complications

I have just visited your car wash in Överby and was treated very badly. I went to the website before my visit and checked that the car wash was open this early in the morning. I was glad that it was almost empty so I didn't have to wait for the vacuum cleaners. I drove in and started vacuuming; I always want to do it before the wash so that the car doesn't get dusty afterwards. After waiting for a while, a woman storms out and starts talking and gesticulating. I can't hear at first because I have my earpods in. I take them out and meet her who is very upset and tells me sharply that "vacuum cleaning is only for customers"! I don't really understand because I am a customer and I explain it to her. She says that we can't have people who just drive in and vacuum and drive away without paying. I explain that I am a customer and I am supposed to wash the car after the vacuuming. She says they want customers to wash their cars first and vacuum afterwards - because otherwise they can't know if you're going to skip. I explain that I always vacuum first and then wash because I don't want the car to get dusty afterwards. She understands the situation and says it's OK for me to drive into the car wash afterwards but continues to angrily tell me about everyone who vacuums and skips, washcloths that get stolen, etc. Why should I have to listen to that?! I point out that I don't appreciate being jumped on like this when I'm a regular customer who intended to do the right thing for me. She says several times, however, that "you have to understand that, that we'll tell you". No, I don't.

I've been washing my car here for several years and am always completely satisfied. This was the last time, though. I'll have to look for another place that really is a "nice car wash" as it says on your sign.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am writing this so that other consumers will be careful and avoid going through what we have experienced.

We bought a car from Erlandsson Bil and about 20 minutes after we received the car on February 26, the engine light came on while driving. Since then, the car has been in for repair four times for the same recurring problem. For most of the time, the car has been in the workshop or has been unusable and we have barely been able to use it since the purchase.

Despite several repair attempts, the problems continued, and we never received any clear documentation of what work was actually carried out, despite our requesting this on several occasions. At the last repair, it was stated that the timing chain had been replaced, but still without any documentation or update in the service book being shown. That is also why we finally requested to cancel the purchase, since we no longer had any confidence in how the car or the matter was handled.

When we picked up the car after the last repair, we also discovered that our front tires had been replaced with worn-out used tires of a different size without our consent or without being informed. If we had not discovered this ourselves, we would never have received any information at all.

When we contacted the company directly and asked what had happened to the tires, we were initially told that they did not know anything and that the car had been to an external workshop. We were told that they would get back to us on Monday with an answer and send documentation for the timing chain replacement and previous repairs, but no response was received.

Only after we contacted them again did they state that the tires had been replaced due to a puncture. We believe that it is unacceptable for changes to be made to a customer's car without consent or information. If an external workshop carried out the work, this does not change the company's responsibility towards us as customers.

After the workshop visit, the car also had new problems, including vibrations in the steering wheel and problems with the steering.

We also did an E-check at Bilprovningen where several error codes and communication errors were discovered in the car, which further showed that the problems were still not resolved.

To check the condition of the car, an independent E-check was performed at Bilprovningen on May 20, 2026. The protocol shows several active error codes as well as serious communication errors in the car's electrical system, including U0100, U1000, C1A26 and C1705. This indicates that the error has not been permanently fixed, even though the car has been in for repair on four occasions.

The loaner cars we received were also in very poor condition. One of the cars had very poor brakes and the front axle shook so much that the car felt unsafe to drive. I informed the company immediately when I returned the car that I did not feel safe driving it because the brakes barely worked at all and I had to press the brake pedal almost all the way to the floor without the car braking normally.

The second loaner car also had very worn and dry tires, which made me feel concerned about safety and was afraid that the tires might burst while driving. Both loaner cars were also cars that the company had for sale.

The whole situation has affected us enormously both financially, practically and psychologically. We have lost time, money and security and feel completely exhausted after the whole process.

We tried to resolve everything calmly and correctly directly with the company for several months. We gave them several chances to fix the problems and finally requested to cancel the purchase, but without receiving any reasonable solution.

After going through this ourselves, we have also found several other people who have described similar experiences with the same company on various pages and forums. Therefore, we feel it is important to share our own experience publicly so that other consumers can be careful and make a careful assessment before purchasing.

Everything we write can be supported by pictures, messages and documentation from our process.

one_star_reviews.text:
STIHL customer service has destroyed our trust in the brand

I have been closely involved in my wife's attempt to return a pair of saw protection trousers purchased directly from STIHL, and the experience has honestly been very disappointing.

We have used and purchased STIHL products for our forestry property for many years and have generally had great respect for the brand and the quality of their equipment. Therefore, it is particularly surprising to experience a customer service where it has been practically impossible to get in touch with the company regarding a simple return.

The return label did not work, emails and contact forms were not answered, and telephone contact led nowhere.

As a customer, you naturally expect that errors can occur. The problem is not the error itself, but the lack of help, contact and responsibility afterwards.

After this experience, I personally will no longer consider buying directly from STIHL.

STIHL customer service is a disaster – never buy directly from them.

We bought a pair of saw protection trousers for around 3,500 SEK directly from STIHL. The trousers were too big, and then a return case began that is still not resolved.

Via STIHL's own customer service we received a return form through their return system at GLS. The package was sent according to the instructions – but was returned by GLS because there was missing information in the return.

Then the real problem began: it is practically impossible to get in touch with STIHL.

We have contacted customer service at both STIHL Denmark and STIHL Sweden via contact form and email. No response. We have also tried calling several times, but the phone system sends you around menus without the possibility of reaching customer service.

In the end, we sent the package with tracking from Sweden at our own expense. Now it seems to be at a delivery point in Stenkullen instead of at STIHL – and still no one can be reached.

The result is saw protection trousers for around 3,500 SEK, a return period that is about to expire and a company that is impossible to communicate with when problems arise.

STIHL may be a premium brand when it comes to products. However, the customer service is far below the level you should expect.

Please buy STIHL from a reputable dealer – but avoid buying directly from STIHL.

⚠️Big disappointment – ​​not genuine Swedish meatballs ⚠️

We visited Kometen in Gothenburg to try their classic meatballs, but unfortunately the experience was a big disappointment.

The meatballs we got did not taste at all like Swedish meatballs usually do. The consistency was spongy and floury, they almost fell apart and had very little feeling of meat or classic Swedish home cooking. Even the gravy tasted strange and nothing felt quite right, apart from the mashed potatoes, lingonberries and cucumber.

We tried to explain to the staff how we experienced the food, but no one really seemed to want to investigate the matter further or try to understand why we reacted the way we did. Instead, we got the feeling that our opinions were mostly dismissed with the comment:
“This is how our meatballs taste.”

What made the experience even more disappointing was that the service was perceived as impersonal and defensive instead of professional and solution-oriented. One would have liked someone to at least take the time to check with the kitchen or try to understand why the food was perceived so badly.

Given the restaurant's reputation, price level, and how much the restaurant markets its meatballs, we expected significantly better quality and service.

Unfortunately, we left the restaurant feeling that the experience was more suited to tourists than genuine Swedish home cooking.

one_star_reviews.text:
I had a disappointing experience here, mainly due to a lack of clarity and communication about prices.

Outside the salon there is a sign (see picture) stating that treatments performed by students from hairdressing school cost 150 SEK. However, there is no other visible price information, either outside or inside the premises, that shows what a regular haircut costs. Based on this, it is reasonable to assume that what is offered here is mainly student haircuts at that price.

As a background, I do not speak fluent Swedish, but I have lived here for a while and understand enough to understand what the sign says. So the problem is not that I did not understand it, but that there was a lack of additional information explaining that there are different options with different prices.

When I entered, I was not given an explanation or asked if I wanted a student haircut or a regular haircut. I was just asked to sit down and the haircut began.

After about an hour, I was charged 500 SEK. This came as a surprise as the only clearly stated price was 150 SEK. Such a large price difference should have been clearly communicated in advance.

It was also unclear who was a “student”. There were two people cutting hair, with no information or clear marking as to who was a student and who was not.

When I brought this up afterwards, the focus was repeatedly on the fact that the sign was in Swedish and that Swedish speakers would understand it. I understand that we are in Sweden, but even my wife, who is Swedish, found the pricing unclear and had not expected such a large difference. So the problem is not about language, but about a lack of clear and transparent information.

To be fair, I have nothing against the person who cut my hair. However, the overall experience was negatively affected by how the situation was handled. There was no clear understanding of the lack of information, and the focus on language made the situation unnecessarily frustrating.

Maybe I should have double-checked beforehand, but clear pricing and basic communication should be a given.

I won't be back. If you are thinking of going here, I recommend that you clearly confirm the service and price before you start.

Pizza + sauce + salad + drink cost 100 SEK when they opened. Now the prices have been raised significantly. I paid 160 SEK for the same menu, and that was during lunchtime. Tastes good, but it's not worth the price.

A completely incompetent administration that took many attempts over several weeks to even produce a digital document to sign to get a place. Responds to emails maybe within a week sometimes if you are not ignored. Pretends that holiday marking is not an indication of what times your child needs care and what not. Minimal work and thinking seems to be the watchword in the office.
Too bad because the daycare workers are good but everything around is crap. I suspect that the municipality's operations in Mölndal are at a more even level.

I needed a certificate for the Norwegian Maritime Directorate as I can no longer work as a cook
I got hold of a doctor in Borås who claimed to be able to write certificates for seamen in Norway called Ladulaas in Borås.

I called them and introduced myself as I always do
- I work as a cook on a ship in Norway and explained to her what certificate I needed - Loss of license and that certificate is on the Norwegian Maritime Directorate's website.
When we had contact by phone before I left, I asked the doctor if she was sure she could arrange this certificate?
so that I wouldn't drive up to Borås (7.5 hours by car) unnecessarily, she replied
- I can arrange all the certificates that are available for Norway.
I paid 1500 SEK for petrol and 2000 SEK for the certificate.
When I got back home, it turned out that the certificate was far from what my office wanted.
I wrote her an email that the certificate was wrong, and that she could make a new certificate.
Then she admits that she does not make certificates for seafarers working in Norway.

When I asked for my 2000 kr for the certificate back, she refuses to pay it back because she claims she has expenses and has also spent time on the certificate that was wrong.

She also says that I got a discount of 1900 kr,

So I should be happy that I am not being cheated out of 3900?

It is her responsibility as a doctor to find out what she can and cannot fix before the patient comes.

I was completely clear with my information to her about what kind of certificate the worker needed.

What kind of morals do they have?

I was completely cheated by her.

As a sick leaver I am quite poor and I felt it in my wallet when I threw 3500 SEK straight into the lake, she refuses to pay me back and wishes me luck in finding someone who can help me with my certificate.

Is it really going to be like this?

No morals at all!

7.5 hours in the car and 3500 SEK poorer
I absolutely do not recommend these Ladulaas to anyone.

It is clear in retrospect that the system is being phased out, but this has not been clearly communicated in connection with the price change. In practice, this means that we as customers are expected to accept higher costs for a solution that is also being phased out.

I would like to raise serious concerns about my experience at Halmstad University, specifically in the Master’s programme in Industrial Management and Innovation.

The academic and administrative environment in this programme has been extremely disappointing. In a class of only 21 students, groups were assigned with 5 members each. However, there was no proper monitoring or guidance from the teachers. As a result, students formed their own groups, and one student was completely excluded and isolated.

What is more concerning is that this student faced teasing and a lack of support from peers, even from students of the same country. When the issue was reported to the student council, no action was taken, and the response was that they could not help in this matter. Even more troubling, the teacher also did not intervene and instead contributed to the negative environment.

Additionally, there have been serious issues with academic fairness and communication. One teacher was frequently absent and failed the student. Later, the same teacher asked the student to redo the work on a different topic, promising better marks. Despite completing the work again, the student has still not received the results. Even after sending numerous emails over three semesters, there has been no response or resolution.

This situation raises serious questions about accountability, student support, and academic standards. For international students, especially those who depend on education loans and financial support from their families, delays like being told to “complete it next year” are not practical or acceptable.

This experience has caused significant stress, financial burden, and uncertainty about the future. It is deeply concerning that such issues are not addressed in a reputed institution.

I hope this feedback highlights the need for better management, fair evaluation, and stronger student support systems…

Your management has already ruined one student’s life. Nothing can change it now, but thank you for your response.

Not a good university for fee-paying international students. It promotes itself as highly international, but the reality feels different. Many master’s programs are heavily concentrated with students from a few countries, like India and Pakistan, so the “international environment” often feels more like marketing than reality.

The teaching quality was disappointing, and most lecturers seemed out of touch with industry standards or practical knowledge.

For students hoping to build a career after graduation, the value is questionable. Job opportunities in Sweden are limited, and the university’s teaching and reputation do not seem strong enough to offset that challenge.

If you are paying large tuition fees, think carefully before choosing this place. There are better universities, better study destinations and better ways to invest your money and time. Sweden is a nice country, but this university did not live up to the image it promotes.

Uncertainties during service: On one occasion I was told that a fog light was broken. Workmanship flaws: The last time I had the wheels balanced, the rims were left dirty, and the balance weights came loose shortly afterwards.

It's sad to have to leave this rating after so many years, but as a customer I expect both technical accuracy and transparency.

Promises a price. Then it becomes a completely different one. Had an offer for basic vaccination for a cat. The first vaccination was done as agreed. AFTER the second was completed, an additional charge of 340 SEK came. The person who picked up our cat, paid nicely.

When pointing out the error, they didn't understand anything. Then the manager called and claimed that NO prices can be promised by anyone other than her. Not even those in the price list. The staff showed clear signs of being afraid of the manager.

I also found out from the manager that my other animals were no longer welcome here. This despite the fact that this place claims to be a so-called district veterinarian. When I complained, the manager threatened me with a police report for defamation. (Note that there is no legal basis for defamation of companies.) Unfortunately, time ran out to file a report with ARN.

I asked TWO different employees about the price for the follow-up vaccination of our cat TWICE on different occasions, and got the same answer from both. Completely without the 340 kronor that was later added.

My impression is that the manager started the business entirely to maximize profits. Shabby premises and lower wages out in the country, as well as somewhat arbitrary prices, are not trustworthy, but in the veterinary industry, most pet owners are in an emergency situation, and do not dare to question what it costs.

At the first visit, which concerned the same cat whose eye was mildly infected, more than ten items ended up on the invoice. Everything from the cost (200?) to write a prescription, to small pieces of paper to wash the eye, which cost 8 kronor each.

Now we have found competent and pleasant veterinarians, for all our animals, elsewhere.

Avoid this veterinarian. Sooner or later your animal will be mistreated, and if you complain…

But if you want to pay more than you get, you've come to the right place.

The next day we knew we wanted to go back in the afternoon to enjoy the sun, atmosphere, and have some drinks and food at our new Favourite venue! . We arrived and the lady at the desk directed us to an area to sit and said our waitress would be with us soon! An older lady approached and we kindly asked if we could sit at a particular empty table in the sun, which had dirty glasses from a previous customer, she didn’t speak but vocally huffed & puffed as she abruptly grabbed the past customers drinks and quickly wiped the table and left! We are tourists in the city and as I don’t drink alcohol I always carry this particular teabag and ask kindly the server at any restaurant if they don’t stock it, if I could use mine but will still pay full price, plus while ordering other food off the menu. I believe this is misleading.

I would like to thank the optician who worked very carefully with the eye examination and the measurement of the lenses for my glasses.

I have cataracts in my eye and I experience something that looks like small ants moving left and right in my field of vision, along with strong light sensitivity.

I chose to have an OCT, 3D scan of the retina and paid 200 kronor for the examination to get a printed result with details that could help me understand the causes of what I am feeling.

What happened afterwards was that I only received a payment receipt that looked like a regular receipt from a grocery store.

I asked the person who gave me the payment receipt:
"Where is the report or result from the OCT, 3D scan of the retina?"

The answer I received was only:
The cataract is small.

I explained that I had chosen and paid for this examination to get more in-depth information and a result.

But the answer remained: “The cataract is small.”

Why didn’t the employee give me a printed report with the results of the examination?

Is it reasonable that a single word – “Small” – should be considered the entire result of the examination?

Why wasn’t I informed before payment that I wouldn’t receive a printed report or any detailed results after the examination?

Second part:

I already use glasses in very good condition with thin lenses that are adapted for astigmatism.

Therefore, I asked the staff to check the frame and then insert the new lenses instead of the old ones.

The employee’s answer was a direct no, without even any check, and that I would have to buy a new frame.

Very bad experience and it will be the last time I visit this place.

I have just visited your car wash in Överby and was treated very badly. I went to the website before my visit and checked that the car wash was open this early in the morning. I was glad that it was almost empty so I didn't have to wait for the vacuum cleaners. I drove in and started vacuuming; I always want to do it before the wash so that the car doesn't get dusty afterwards. After waiting for a while, a woman storms out and starts talking and gesticulating. I can't hear at first because I have my earpods in. I take them out and meet her who is very upset and tells me sharply that "vacuum cleaning is only for customers"! I don't really understand because I am a customer and I explain it to her. She says that we can't have people who just drive in and vacuum and drive away without paying. I explain that I am a customer and I am supposed to wash the car after the vacuuming. She says they want customers to wash their cars first and vacuum afterwards - because otherwise they can't know if you're going to skip. I explain that I always vacuum first and then wash because I don't want the car to get dusty afterwards. She understands the situation and says it's OK for me to drive into the car wash afterwards but continues to angrily tell me about everyone who vacuums and skips, washcloths that get stolen, etc. Why should I have to listen to that?! I point out that I don't appreciate being jumped on like this when I'm a regular customer who intended to do the right thing for me. She says several times, however, that "you have to understand that, that we'll tell you". No, I don't.

I've been washing my car here for several years and am always completely satisfied. This was the last time, though. I'll have to look for another place that really is a "nice car wash" as it says on your sign.

PS Nowhere does it say that you have to wash first and then vacuum.

I advise all dog owners not to take a course at the dog academy.
The instructors do not base the course content on modern science and many of the methods are based on physical violence.
For example, we course participants were instructed to use a choke chain on the dogs and to correct the dog by jerking when it pulled on the leash. If the dog did not show clear submission in the form of ears lying back, a low posture and the tail between the legs, the handler has not corrected his dog hard enough and must act more forcefully.
On one occasion, we witnessed a course participant who pushed his dog down and lay on top of it when it did not listen to a command and where the instructor urged the course participant to hold the dog in that position for a longer time to ensure that the dog really felt that it was being punished. The communication from the instructors was very manipulative and there was absolutely no pleasant atmosphere. During the theoretical parts, many examples were also given of situations where physical violence and punishments were used. For example, one instructor tells of having had to correct her own dog "properly" on various occasions and that she even staged a situation with the aim of punishing her dog. Then she had put out a sandwich, shown the dog the sandwich, walked away and with the help of a mirror saw when the dog was about to take it and then flew at the dog and physically grabbed it and she herself describes how scared the dog became at that incident without feeling any remorse, shame or understanding of why it is very problematic to act in that way.
There was also talk of how the instructors had "helped" another team with their reactive dog by throwing a can full of gravel at it. Unfortunately, the list is long and these are just a few examples of the disgusting methods the dog academy advocates.
Fortunately, I know better myself, of course we questioned the methods and absolutely did not subject our dog to any of these abuses. Unfortunately, the instructors were also not familiar with the terminology of basic learning theory, research, or willing to discuss/consider research, so it was impossible to get anywhere. We ultimately chose to simply cancel the course and go home.
If you have a dog and want him or her to feel good, whether it's training or upbringing, choose another place, absolutely don't go here! There is no reason whatsoever why you should have to use force to achieve either upbringing or obedience.

Hi,

I placed an order with Toolab￼ on May 7th — a tool kit and some smaller accessories, for a total of about 15,000 SEK. It wasn’t a huge order, but the tools were needed for a job outside the city where I live.

What’s very frustrating is that the entire order was left waiting for a small detail that I didn’t even need urgently. Today I have to go to the job site, but the tools won’t arrive until Monday. And this despite two phone calls during the week. After the first call, nothing happened at all — the order wasn’t split up and wasn’t shipped.

Now I’m forced to borrow tools from friends because what I ordered almost two weeks ago still hasn’t arrived.

Unfortunately, I feel like this has become very common in Sweden. You see “delivery 2–5 days” on the website, but in practice you often have to wait significantly longer. It feels like orders are being held back to coordinate deliveries and reduce costs, instead of sending what’s actually in stock right away.

For those of us who work with tools, this is not just an annoyance — it costs money. Tools are what I work with and earn my living from. When deliveries don't work, you lose work time and income.

The most disappointing thing is perhaps the lack of accountability. No apology, no compensation, no solution despite the problem being brought to our attention several times.

Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this store after this experience, and I will not shop here again. I will also not recommend the company to others in the industry, as delays like these create downtime and costs for businesses.

Not recommended if you value security, fixed prices and transparent contracts.

I was in advanced discussions with this agency to hire them for my company's accounting. At first glance, their prices may look competitive, but when you examine their contract terms in depth, a very unsafe picture emerges for you as a customer.

According to my strong experience and analysis, their business model is structured to attract customers with low base prices, but the contracts are full of legal loopholes, ambiguities and vague wording. They leave the door wide open to be able to add hidden system costs, percentage increases and expensive hourly rates afterwards. In addition, they were extremely unwilling to guarantee in the contract that they take 100% financial responsibility for penalties from the Swedish Tax Agency if they themselves make a mistake.

When I, as an entrepreneur, refused to accept vague terms and instead made strict, professional demands for total transparency – I demanded exact figures and a watertight agreement where all risks and costs were clarified in advance – they chose to completely withdraw and withdraw their quote.

My impression is crystal clear: When an accounting firm withdraws from a deal simply because the client demands exact prices and a clear responsibility relationship, then the relationship is not built on the client's security. It seems that they would rather keep a legal space for themselves in order to be able to invoice hidden fees in the future.

If you want to run your business without worrying about invisible costs and want an accounting firm that stands by its work with straight pipes – look no further. Here, there is a great risk that what looks cheap on the surface will ultimately be an expensive and frustrating story.
